en.title: Sweet Hour of Prayer
en.author: William W. Walford
stanzas:
[D]Sweet hour of prayer! sweet [G]hour of prayer!
That [D]calls me from a [A]world of care,
And [D]bids me at my [G]Father's throne
Make [D]all my wants and [A7]wishes [D]known.
In [D]seasons of distress and grief,
My soul has often found re[A]lief,
And [D]oft escaped the [G]tempter's snare,
By [D]thy return, sweet [A7]hour of [D]prayer!

Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
The joys I feel, the bliss I share,
Of those whose anxious spirits burn
With strong desires for thy return!
With such I hasten to the place
Where God my Savior shows His face,
And gladly take my station there,
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer!

Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
Thy wings shall my petition bear
To Him whose truth and faithfulness
Engage the waiting soul to bless.
And since He bids me seek His face,
Believe His Word and trust His grace,
I'll cast on Him my every care,
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer!

Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
May I thy consolation share,
Till, from Mount Pisgah's lofty height,
I view my home and take my flight.
This robe of flesh I'll drop, and rise
To seize the everlasting prize,
And shout, while passing through the air,
"Farewell, farewell, sweet hour of prayer!"

notes: Text from Timeless Truths (Evening Light Songs #312, Select Hymns #528), four stanzas. Hymnary's representative text (United Methodist Hymnal) prints three, dropping stanza 4 ('May I thy consolation share'), which its notes say is sometimes omitted; the three it has agree with TT word for word apart from lower-case pronouns and line openings and one comma. All four ship. Author William W. Walford, 1845 (the attribution rests on Thomas Salmon's 1845 account; hymnary carries the same). Tune: hymnary files it under its first line, '[Sweet hour of prayer, sweet hour of prayer] (Bradbury)', and most hymnals name it SWEET HOUR; meter 8.8.8.8 D (L.M.D.). Key: hymnary's instances run 36 D to 25 C; TT prints D, already a guitar key. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat. Each 'sweet hour of prayer' pair is I then IV; the one-beat IV the inner voices make on 'dis-' of 'distress' and 'of-' of 'often' was dropped, as were the sus4 neighbours over the pedal and a vii-dim7 of V before each cadence. The cadences are I6/4-V7-I, written A7 then D.
